subject: rquesting help with an issue looping plots: y in aes seems to be a pointer when subseting using variables

messages.author: a0bead3a85f4f46a
messages.subject: rquesting help with an issue looping plots: y in aes seems to be a pointer when subseting using variables
parts:
Could someone enlight me on the following issue? 

Seems that when storing a plot in an object and the aes is given as a subindexing using a variable, the variable gets interpolated not when storing the object but when printing it. Is that true?

I am looping through a list of variables in order to make a multiplot with ggplot, storing all the resulting plots in a list, like.

p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev, labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot() + labs(x="groups", y=i)

where y is obtained as 'datxx[,i]))'

When I do the plots by hand giving the x and y with the 'name' of the column of the dataframe, things are  OK, but (as in the previous example) when I pass the index of the column in a variable an therefore using in the aes the full dataframe subindexing notation, then all the plots stored in the list become the same for the data(but not the axes labels). Seems that the plot objects only calls the code for plotting at printing time, so the variable used in the subindexing takes the value at printing time instead of using the corresponding value in each pass of the loop. I can be wrong.

In the attachment I show a graph for loop with value2 where the y label is 2 but the data points are all 1 (because I run loop with value1 the last one).


I assume that this is intended and is a feature of ggplot so I would appreciate if someone can:

A)  point me to the corresponding documentation or an explanation of this feature in order to prevent data bugs in my results in the future.

B) Which is one correct way for storing the plots in a list generated in a loop in a static way?. Probably the solution is in front of my eyes but unfortunately seems that after exploring this issue for several hours and reduced it to the following test example I am blocked going in circles with this problem.

reproducible example:

library(ggplot2)
 datxx<- data.frame(a=rep(1,9), b=rep(2,9), c=rep(3,9), y=rep(1:3,each=3))
 datxx_fact <- data.frame(lev=1:3,lab=c('x','y','z'))
 p<- list()
# controlling hte loop by hand
 i=2;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev, labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+ labs(x="groups", y=i)
 i=1;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev, labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+ labs(x="groups", y=i)
 p[[2]]
# here p[[2]] plots the values corresponding to i==1 see attachment !!!

i=2;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev, labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+ labs(x="groups", y=i)
p[[2]]
# here as p[[2]] has been printed when i has the same value that when created,  the plot is correct


Thanks

Pablo

Probably the best description is in section 4.5 of the ggplot book where
it talks about the right hand side of aes declarations being variables
that are evaluated in the context of the data arguments (either to the
layer or overall plot) and that they should not reference vectors
outside of that.

> B) Which is one correct way for storing the plots in a list generated in a
> loop in a static way?. Probably the solution is in front of my eyes but
> unfortunately seems that after exploring this issue for several hours and
> reduced it to the following test example I am blocked going in circles with
> this problem.
>
> reproducible example:

> library(ggplot2)
> datxx<- data.frame(a=rep(1,9), b=rep(2,9), c=rep(3,9), y=rep(1:3,each=3))
> datxx_fact <- data.frame(lev=1:3,lab=c('x','y','z'))
> p<- list()
> # controlling hte loop by hand
> i=2;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev,
> labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+ labs(x="groups", y=i)
> i=1;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=factor(y, levels=datxx_fact$lev,

> labels=datxx_fact$lab), y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+ labs(x="groups", y=i)
> p[[2]]
> # here as p[[2]] has been printed when i has the same value that when
> created, the plot is correct

I'll walk through improvements.

First, put everything needed into a single data.frame; you don't
want/need to be referencing datxx_fact separately from datxx

datxx$yf <- factor(datxx$y, levels=datxx_fact$lev, labels=datxx_fact$lab)

Now there is a separate column in datxx which contains the transformed
variable that keeps appearing as your x aesthetic. This simplifies your
code to:

p<- list()
i=2;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=yf, y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+
labs(x="groups", y=i)
i=1;p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes(x=yf, y=datxx[,i]))+geom_boxplot()+
labs(x="groups", y=i)

(but doesn't fix your problem). The problem persists because datxx[,i]
is not evaluated until later and the value of i is not stored until that
time (but the current value of i is used when it is printed). One way
around this is to use a different version of aes which evaluates
"sooner": aes_string specifies the mapping using the names of the
columns as strings, not symbols.

i=2; p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes_string(x="yf", y=names(datxx)[i])) +
geom_boxplot() + labs(x="groups", y=i)
i=1; p[[i]] <- ggplot(datxx, aes_string(x="yf", y=names(datxx)[i])) +
geom_boxplot() + labs(x="groups", y=i)

This gives different plots for the two elements of p, and neither
depends on the value of i in the global environment at the time that p
is printed. I don't think the difference in when arguments are evaluated
between aes and aes_string is documented anywhere (or even if it
deliberately different).

A further refinement would be to melt the data and use plyr functions to
subset it, passing each piece to a ggplot call in turn.

library("reshape2")
datxxm <- melt(datxx, id.vars=c("y","yf"))

library("plyr")
p <- dlply(datxxm, .(variable), function(DF) {
ggplot(DF, aes(x=yf, y=value)) + geom_boxplot() + labs(x="groups",
y=unique(DF$variable))
})

If you really don't want to melt the data, you can effectively loop over
either column names or column indexes and use the aes_string approach.
These all work and differ in how the y label is determined. The last one
corresponds most to your example.

p <- llply(setNames(names(datxx)[1:2], names(datxx)[1:2]), function(n) {
ggplot(datxx, aes_string(x="yf", y=n)) + geom_boxplot() +
labs(x="groups", y=n)
})

p <- alply(1:2, 1, function(n) {
ggplot(datxx, aes_string(x="yf", y=names(datxx)[n])) + geom_boxplot()
+ labs(x="groups", y=n)
})
